title: Implicit Differentiation
lead: An equation in x and y can define y as a function of x implicitly, without solving for it. Implicit differentiation differentiates both sides of such an equation, treating y as a function of x, and so finds the slope of a tangent line to curves such as a circle, the folium of Descartes and an ellipse.
objectives: Find the derivative of a complicated function by using implicit differentiation.
Use implicit differentiation to determine the equation of a tangent line.
summary_html:
• We use implicit differentiation to find derivatives of implicitly defined functions (functions defined by equations).
  • By using implicit differentiation, we can find the equation of a tangent line to the graph of a curve.

exercises.prompt: Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ for $y$ defined implicitly by the equation $4x^{5}+\tan y=y^{2}+5x.$

answer.hint: Follow the problem solving strategy, remembering to apply the chain rule to differentiate $\tan$ and $y^{2}.$

exercises.prompt:
For the equation $x^{2}+2xy-3y^{2}=0,$

a. Find an equation of the normal to the tangent line at the point $(1,1).$

b. At what other point does the normal line in a. intersect the graph of the equation?

For the equation $x^{2}+xy+y^{2}=7,$

a. Find the $x$-intercept(s).

b. Find the slope of the tangent line(s) at the x-intercept(s).

c. What does the value(s) in b. indicate about the tangent line(s)?

answer.solution: a. $(\pm \sqrt{7},0)$ b. $-2$ c. They are parallel since the slope is the same at both intercepts.

exercises.prompt: Find an equation of the tangent line to the graph of the equation ${\tan }^{-1}(x+y)=x^{2}+\frac{\pi}{4}$ at the point $(0,1).$

[T] The number of cell phones produced when $x$ dollars is spent on labor and $y$ dollars is spent on capital invested by a manufacturer can be modeled by the equation $60x^{3/4}y^{1/4}=3240.$

a. Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ and evaluate at the point $(81,16).$

b. Interpret the result of a.

answer.solution: a. $-0.5926$ b. When ＄81 is spent on labor and ＄16 is spent on capital, the amount spent on capital is decreasing by ＄0.5926 per ＄1 spent on labor.
